items.title: Reply - Letter to the Editor - "Biological aging or dietary biomarkers? Interpreting associations between dietary patterns and biological age acceleration".
Clinical impact of blood loss during mechanical thrombus aspiration for pulmonary embolism intervention, a sub-analysis of the USAT IH-PE registry.
items.abstract: The clinical impact and critical threshold of intraprocedural blood loss (BL) during large-bore aspiration thrombectomy for pulmonary embolism (PE) remain poorly defined. This study evaluates how blood loss influences major bleeding events and in-hospital mortality. We analysed 104 patients undergoing aspiration thrombectomy for PE in the USAT IH-PE registry with recorded intraprocedural blood loss (mL). Outcomes were major bleeding (BARC ≥3), death and a composite endpoint. Exploratory analyses were repeated, stratified by pre-procedural Hb (<11 vs ≥11 g/dL). Median blood loss was 300 mL; bleeding occurred in 21%, death in 7% and the composite endpoint in 22%. Blood loss correlated only weakly with the Hb drop and not after adjustment. It was higher in patients with major bleeding (380 ± 121 mL vs 289 ± 122 mL, AUC 0.72; OR 1.74 per +100 mL) and the composite endpoint (358 ± 116 mL vs 293 ± 127 mL, AUC 0.67), but unrelated to mortality. In an exploratory subgroup analysis, the association with major bleeding appeared stronger in patients with Hb <11 g/dL (n = 22; AUC 0.93). Independent predictors of the composite endpoint were blood loss (aOR 2.18, 1.35-3.52, p = 0.001), lower pre-procedural Hb (aOR 0.65, 0.48-0.89, p = 0.006) and high-risk PE (aOR 12.01, 3.42-42.25, p < 0.001). In the full cohort, a ≥ 280 mL threshold predicted major bleeding with 91% sensitivity and 95% negative predictive value. Results were consistent after adjustment for device type. Intraprocedural blood loss independently predicts bleeding and adverse outcomes after aspiration thrombectomy for PE, possibly more so in anaemic patients, and a ≥ 280 mL threshold may support risk stratification.

items.title: Beta-blocker continuation versus interruption during transcatheter aortic valve implantation: Rationale and design of the BETA-TAVI randomized trial.
items.abstract: Beta-blockers are common in patients referred for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but there is no consensus on whether they should be continued through the procedure. Continuation could worsen bradycardia or atrioventricular block in a setting already prone to conduction injury, whereas interruption may provoke adrenergic rebound, tachyarrhythmia, myocardial ischemia, or hemodynamic instability. Available evidence is observational and does not resolve this trade-off. BETA-TAVI is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, open-label, randomized noninferiority trial in adults with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI while receiving chronic oral beta-blocker therapy. Participants are randomized 1:1 to continuation of their usual beta-blocker or interruption from 72 h before TAVI through day 7. The primary endpoint is new permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) within 7 days. Secondary endpoints include high-degree atrioventricular block, new conduction disturbances, atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, severe bradycardia, hemodynamic deterioration, mortality, and later PPI. The calculated sample size is 348 participants. The prespecified noninferiority margin is 6.5 percentage points on the absolute risk-difference scale; the primary conclusion requires concordant modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses. BETA-TAVI tests a frequent but poorly studied medication decision using a randomized strategy comparison. The trial will determine whether chronic beta-blocker therapy can be continued through TAVI without a clinically unacceptable increase in early permanent pacing and will characterize the arrhythmic and hemodynamic consequences of both strategies. gov identifier: NCT05721170.

items.title: Additional value of optical coherence tomography-fractional flow reserve for the optimization of percutaneous coronary intervention.
items.abstract: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) optimization remains largely driven by intravascular imaging, potentially leading to overtreatment of functionally irrelevant findings. To compare the impact of optical coherence tomography (OCT), angiography-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR angio ), and the integration of imaging and physiology (OCT-FFR) on post-PCI optimization strategies. Among patients included in the AQVA-I and II trials, we selected those receiving post-PCI OCT (n = 79). Physiology reconstruction based on OCT traces was obtained in 76 OCT runs. One operator, blinded to the post-PCI optimization procedural plan and to final PCI result, planned the procedure according to FFR angio , OCT and OCT-FFR. The primary endpoint was the rate of any additional post-PCI optimization maneuver. Secondary endpoints included type of optimization strategy and pairwise differences between modalities. Among 79 patients, 76 had complete triplet data. The rate of any additional post-PCI optimization was highest with OCT (33/76, 43.4%), followed by OCT-FFR (26/76, 34.2%) and lowest with FFR angio (5/76, 6.6%) (overall p < 0.001). The overall rate of any additional maneuver was not significantly different between OCT and OCT-FFR (absolute paired difference 2.6%; adjusted p = 0.500). Recommendations for edge dissection stenting, post-dilation for stent underexpansion, and post-dilation for malapposition were identical between OCT and OCT-FFR. In contrast, additional stenting of adjacent segments was reduced with OCT-FFR compared with OCT (4/76 [5.3%] vs 12/76 [15.8%]) and was recommended at the same rate as with FFRangio (4/76 [5.3%]). OCT guidance is associated with a higher rate of post-PCI optimization maneuvers compared with FFR angio , reflecting its sensitivity to morphological abnormalities. Integration of functional assessment through OCT-FFR significantly reduces additional stenting in segments defined as 5 mm proximal and distal to the stent edges, while preserving treatment of clinically relevant mechanical complications.

items.title: Visceral adipose tissue measured by DXA, prevalent cardiovascular disease, and mortality in US adults: cross-sectional and prospective analyses from NHANES 2011-2018.
items.abstract: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) is a metabolically active fat depot closely linked to cardiometabolic risk. Our aim is to evaluate the association between DXA-measured VAT and both prevalent cardiovascular disease and mortality in younger adults. We conducted cross-sectional and prospective analyses using NHANES 2011-2018 data. Adults aged 20-59 with DXA-VAT measurements were included. VAT was analyzed as quartiles and a continuous variable. Prevalent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) was assessed cross-sectionally. All-cause and cardiovascular mortality were evaluated prospectively via National Death Index linkage. Survey-weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were applied. The final cohort included 11,914 people; 440 (3.7%) had prevalent ASCVD, 213 died from any cause, and 44 from cardiovascular causes. Participants in Q4 had higher odds of ASCVD than Q1 (OR 2.12, 1.32-3.38, p = 0.002; p-trend = 0.001). Each 1-SD increase in VAT was linked with OR 1.45 (1.26-1.66, p < 0.001) for ASCVD, persisting after BMI adjustment (OR 1.40, p = 0.001) and further adjustment for mediators (OR 1.24, p = 0.040). Over a median follow-up of 5.1 years, VAT per SD was associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.16; 1.03-1.31; p = 0.018), which attenuated after adjustment for BMI. For cardiovascular mortality, Q4 had an HR of 6.28 (1.95-20.2, p = 0.002) and VAT per SD, an HR of 1.48 (1.16-1.88, p = 0.002). In a nationally representative sample of US adults, higher DXA-measured VAT was associated with prevalent ASCVD and cardiovascular mortality, supporting the potential clinical relevance of assessing visceral adiposity for cardiovascular risk stratification.

items.title: Thresholds and control in a multiscale epidemic model.
items.abstract: We formulated a multiscale epidemic model linking within-host viral dynamics to population transmission under resistance-mediated loss of treatment efficacy. The within-host subsystem tracked target cells, infected cells, viral load, and immune effectors, while an SEIR model represents population spread, vaccination, and recovery. We established positivity and invariance, derived a quasi-steady population model through singular perturbation, and provided a finite-horizon reduction error estimate that included the effects of initial conditions and changes in control. For constant controls and frozen efficacy, a next-generation matrix yielded a control reproduction number and local and global disease-free stability thresholds. A finite-horizon control problem compared vaccination and treatment schedules under progressive efficacy decay, using numerically optimized open-loop policies and explicitly defined baseline controls. In 180-day full-model simulations at baseline resistance, the computed policy had a composite cost of 8623.88, compared with 9638.97 for constant maximal control, while cumulative incidence was 0.240 versus 0.221. A cost-component analysis and a comparison without the explicit viral-load penalty revealed how the objective weights affect these rankings. Under active treatment, resistance influences cumulative incidence, and a synthetic negative-binomial fit reproduces weekly exposure means.

items.title: Immune-nutritional indexes for predicting the response to nivolumab immunotherapy in gastric cancer.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors reportedly improve survival outcomes in patients with gastric cancer (GC). However, most patients develop disease progression, for which treatment options are limited. We examined biomarkers for identification of patients with good response for promising treatment like immune checkpoint inhibitors. We analyzed 40 patients with clinical unresectable or recurrent GC who received nivolumab immunotherapy and divided them into a responder group (n=7) and non-responder group (n=33) based on the RECIST criteria. We prioritized the following biomarkers:nutritional markers (prognostic nutritional index [PNI], lymphocyte-to-plasma C-reactive protein ratio [LCR], and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio [NLR]), sarcopenia, and osteopenia. Our model predicted the response to nivolumab with excellent accuracy in immune-nutritional markers (LCR:area under the curve [AUC]=0.74, NLR:AUC=0.75, PNI:AUC=0.60), osteopenia (AUC=0.83), and sarcopenia (AUC=0.73). Moreover, the predictive accuracy of the risk-assessment model was superior to that of each parameter (AUC=0.93). Univariate Cox proportional hazard regression analysis revealed that our model was an independent predictor of survival outcomes (hazard ratio=3.22, 95% confidence interval=1.62-6.42, P<0.01). Measurement of nutritional markers, osteopenia, and sarcopenia allowed prediction of a response to nivolumab immunotherapy. Our novel risk-assessment model for predicting the response to nivolumab has potential for clinical translation. J. Med. Invest. 73 : 326-333, August, 2026.

items.title: Regulatory T cells in kidney diseases: context-dependent functions and therapeutic potential.
items.abstract: Kidney diseases, including acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), IgA nephropathy (IgAN), lupus nephritis (LN), and kidney transplantation, share features of immune dysregulation, persistent inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central to immune tolerance in the kidney, yet their function is not uniform: it is shaped by developmental origin, disease etiology, disease stage and the metabolic and inflammatory tone of the renal microenvironment. Single-cell and spatially resolved profiling has revealed tissue-resident, activated, dysfunctional, and senescent Treg states in the injured kidney, and has begun to define the renal Treg niche. Building on this evidence, we propose an etiology- and stage-stratified framework in which Tregs protect against acute injury, promote repair, or, under specific conditions, contribute to fibrotic remodeling. This framework rationalizes therapeutic targeting: cytokine and small-molecule Treg expansion (notably low-dose IL-2), Treg-compatible optimization of conventional immunosuppression, adoptive polyclonal and antigen-specific CAR/TCR-Treg therapies, and metabolic or tissue-targeted engineering should be matched to disease etiology and stage. Integrating spatial multi-omics, lineage-stabilizing strategies, and standardized manufacturing and monitoring will be essential to translate Treg-based therapies into precision treatments for kidney diseases.

items.title: Sugar-assisted separation of pectin/polyvinyl alcohol/carbohydrate microneedle patch enabling n-butylidenephthalide/resiquimod Co-delivery for chemo-immunotherapy of glioma.
items.abstract: Intracranial implant displacement may compromise local glioblastoma therapy. We developed detachable pectin/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) hydrogel microneedles (MNs) for localized delivery of n-butylidenephthalide (Bdph) and resiquimod (R848), designed to improve tissue anchoring while limiting residual implanted material. The pectin/PVA hydrogel was dual-crosslinked by freeze-thaw treatment and Ca 2+ -mediated ionic crosslinking using CaCO₃/glucono-δ-lactone (GDL). Sucrose promoted backing-layer disintegration and detachment, whereas mannitol in the MN core supported needle formation and structural integrity. Successfully fabricated MNs penetrated the skin and detached from the backing layer, while Ca 2+ -mediated crosslinking increased the bulk hydrogel tensile strength by approximately 4.2-fold. Within 60 min, backing-layer mass loss exceeded 90% in the presence of pectinase and reached approximately 82% in pectinase-free aqueous medium. Bdph exhibited a relatively sustained release profile, whereas R848 showed more rapid release. Combined R848 and Bdph treatment reduced glioma cell viability in vitro, and repeated concurrent administration of separate R848- and Bdph-loaded MNs produced the greatest tumor growth inhibition among the tested groups in a subcutaneous glioma model. Bdph-containing treatments were associated with increased cleaved caspase-3 and reduced Ki-67 immunoreactivity, whereas the combined treatment showed increased intratumoral CD8 and TNF-α immunoreactivity. Short-term histological evaluations following subcutaneous and intracranial MN application provided preliminary evidence of local and systemic biocompatibility under the tested conditions. Overall, this detachable pectin/PVA hydrogel MN platform supports the feasibility of sequential localized administration of Bdph and R848 and provides a potential strategy for localized chemo-immunotherapy of glioma.

items.title: Perioperative dynamics of selenoproteins and risk of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
items.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) affects over 20% of patients and is associated with perioperative mortality and long-term renal impairment. Reliable early biomarkers remain limited. Selenoproteins, including glutathione peroxidases (GPX1, GPX3) and selenoprotein P (SEPP1), are critical for redox homeostasis, but their perioperative changes in CSA-AKI remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize selenoprotein dynamics and explore their association with renal function and CSA-AKI. In this prospective observational cohort study, 99 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery were enrolled, serum and urine samples were collected preoperatively and at 24/48 h postoperatively. SEPP1, GPX1, GPX3, and KIM-1 were measured. Mixed-effects, correlation, and logistic regression assessed selenoprotein dynamics and associations with CSA-AKI, with an exploratory model including age and preoperative SEPP1. Among 89 analyzed patients, 22 (24.7%) developed AKI. Univariable analyses showed that lower perioperative SEPP1 levels, attenuated urinary SEPP1 increases, and greater serum GPX1 decreases were associated with higher odds of CSA-AKI; older age, hypertension, and longer operation time were also associated with CSA-AKI. Postoperatively, serum SEPP1 declined markedly, remaining lower in AKI patients. Urinary SEPP1 increased significantly in non-AKI patients. Changes in GPX1 and GPX3 differed between AKI and non-AKI groups. Serum SEPP1 correlated positively with eGFR and inversely with creatinine and cystatin C. An exploratory model incorporating age and preoperative serum SEPP1 yielded an apparent AUC of 0.818. In summary, perioperative alterations in selenoproteins (GPX1, GPX3, SEPP1) are closely linked to CSA-AKI. Preoperative SEPP1 combined with clinical variables may enable early risk prediction and support timely intervention. Acute kidney injury is a common complication after cardiac surgery. Selenoproteins help regulate antioxidant defense and responses to physiological stress, but their changes around cardiac surgery are not well understood.In this prospective study of 89 adults undergoing cardiac surgery, 22 developed acute kidney injury. In 54 patients with biomarker measurements, we assessed three selenoproteins—SEPP1, GPX1, and GPX3—in blood and urine before and after surgery.Patients who developed acute kidney injury showed different perioperative selenoprotein patterns, including lower serum SEPP1 levels and altered GPX1 and GPX3 responses. Higher serum SEPP1 was generally associated with better kidney function, and preoperative serum SEPP1 showed potential value for risk assessment when combined with age.These findings suggest that selenoproteins may provide additional information about kidney vulnerability after cardiac surgery. Larger independent studies are needed before these markers can be used clinically.

items.title: Immune-related hepatitis and HLA-DQB1*06:01 as potential predictor biomarkers in East Asian patients with lung cancer treated with ICIs: a large-scale real-world study.
Comprehensive Immunoprofiling and Multi-Omics Modeling Reveal Key Immune Features Associated with Disease Progression and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Comprehensive profiling of peripheral immune cells has shown prognostic and disease-monitoring value across multiple cancers, but its clinical relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly unresectable HCC, remains insufficiently defined. To address this gap, we performed integrated peripheral immunoprofiling combining T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing, flow cytometry-based T-cell phenotyping, bulk RNA sequencing, and public single-cell RNA-seq analysis in healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients. This design enabled characterization of HCC-associated and stage-associated peripheral immune alterations and identification of immunotherapy-relevant features in unresectable HCC. Single-cell analysis and flow cytometry revealed remodeling of circulating T-cell states in unresectable HCC, including reduced naïve-like compartments, enrichment of Treg-like cells, and increased memory/effector differentiation. TCR repertoire analysis showed reduced diversity, increased clonal dominance, altered V-J gene usage, decreased interindividual sharing, and convergent motif-level alterations, with early CD4 + TCR perturbations in resectable HCC and more pronounced CD8 + repertoire restriction in unresectable disease. Exploratory GLIPH-based motif analysis, HLA inference, and peptide-HLA binding prediction suggested candidate motif-HLA antigen associations involving hepatitis virus-derived antigens and recurrent HCC mutation-derived candidate neoantigens, although experimental validation is required. Bulk RNA-seq of peripheral CD8 + T cells revealed higher Activation/Effector function, Exhaustion, and Anergy signature scores in both resectable and unresectable HCC than in HDs, with no significant differences between the two HCC groups, whereas the Chemokine/Chemokine receptor signature was specifically increased in unresectable HCC. The overall IFN-response signature did not differ significantly among the three groups. Integrative machine-learning models were then developed using 818 peripheral immune-related features. Among them, the random forest (RF) model effectively distinguished healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients, with consistently high sensitivity and area under the curve (AUC) in both cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. In unresectable HCC patients receiving immunotherapy, four features derived from TCR-seq and T-cell subset profiling discriminated responders (CR/PR) from non-responders (SD/PD) in univariate analyses, while multivariate prioritization further highlighted ULBP1 as a consistently prioritized response-associated feature that requires validation in an independent cohort. Overall, this study supports comprehensive peripheral immune profiling as an exploratory framework for identifying stage-associated immune alterations and candidate biomarkers to inform personalized immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

items.title: Defining the druggability of viral macrodomains in coronaviruses and alphaviruses.
items.abstract: Viral macrodomains are ADP-ribosylhydrolases encoded within the nonstructural proteins of coronaviruses and alphaviruses-2 RNA virus families with pandemic potential. Genetic studies demonstrate that ADP-ribose binding and ADP-ribosylhydrolase activity are critical for replication in alphaviruses and select coronaviruses, such as Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus and murine hepatitis virus. In contrast, for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus (SARS-CoV) and SARS-CoV-2, this domain primarily enhances in vivo fitness by modulating the innate immune response, establishing the macrodomain as a validated antiviral target. Structure-guided and high-throughput efforts have identified selective inhibitors for SARS-CoV-2 and, more recently, early-stage inhibitors of the alphavirus chikungunya virus. Both exploit a conserved active-site architecture that organizes ligand recognition into adenine, phosphate, ribose, and oxyanion subsites. Despite screening of extensive chemical libraries, inhibitor discovery has repeatedly converged on adenine-anchored scaffolds requiring polar engagement of the oxyanion region to achieve potency. This convergence defines a structurally confined druggable corridor but reveals a persistent permeability-potency tradeoff imposed by the polarity required for catalytic engagement. Cross-family comparisons further demonstrate localized divergence that shapes selectivity and constrains straightforward scaffold portability. Here, we synthesize structural, biochemical, and antiviral advances across SARS-CoV-2 and chikungunya virus, define the current boundaries of macrodomain chemical space, and delineate the chemical and biological constraints that now govern translation of catalytic inhibition into predictable antiviral efficacy. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Viral macrodomains have emerged as compelling antiviral targets in 2 pandemic-potential virus families, coronaviruses and alphaviruses, owing to their conservation and role in virulence. This review defines the chemical space and druggability of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 and chikungunya virus macrodomains and the structural and biological constraints that must be overcome to translate catalytic inhibition into next-generation antivirals.

p53 activates chaperone-mediated autophagy to remodel metabolism and suppress tumorigenesis.
items.abstract: p53 protects against the initiation and progression of cancers, but the mechanisms underlying this function remain incompletely understood. Chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) is a form of autophagy unique in vertebrates, yet its regulation and function are unclear. Here, we demonstrate that p53 functions as a central activator of CMA, integrating stress signals to regulate this selective autophagic pathway. Mechanistically, the energy sensor AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) inhibits CMA by preventing oligomerization of its receptor LAMP2A. Cytoplasmic p53 interacts with AMPK and relieves this inhibition. By activating CMA, p53 promotes lysosomal degradation of isocitrate dehydrogenases IDH1 and IDH2, thereby reducing intracellular α-ketoglutarate levels, inhibiting reductive glutamine metabolism, and suppressing growth of lung and liver cancers. Tumor-associated p53 mutants fail to promote CMA, whereas oncogenic IDH1/2 mutants evade CMA-mediated degradation. These results suggest that CMA activation may be a fundamental component of p53 function, through which it modulates metabolism and inhibits oncogenic growth.

items.title: Liver cancer incidence trends in younger versus older adults over time: an analysis of population-based cancer registry data.
items.abstract: Liver cancer epidemiology is evolving, yet age-specific patterns remain poorly characterized. We aimed to assess variation in age-specific liver cancer incidence trends based on population-based cancer registry data. We extracted annual liver cancer incidence (1978-2017) for 47 countries from Cancer Incidence in Five Continents Plus. Age-standardized incidence rates (ASRs) were compared over time and over the most recent decade for three age-groups (15-49, 50-69, 70 +) using Estimated Annual Percentage Change (EAPC) in 38 populations. From 1978-2017, ASRs declined in high-incidence countries in Eastern and South-Eastern Asia but increased in low-incidence countries across Northern America, Australia/New Zealand, and Northern Europe. During 2008-2017, ASRs among younger adults (15-49) declined in 11 of 38 male populations (EAPC -10.0% in France) and in females in the Republic of Korea (-3.7%) and China (-2.6%). In older adults (50-69 and 70 +), ASRs declined in high-incidence countries (Republic of Korea, Japan, China) during 2008-2017, while increasing in 15 male populations and 11 female populations (age 50-69) and in 12 male populations and 10 female populations (age 70 +), mostly in Northern and Western Europe and Northern America. Overall, trends in hepatocellular carcinoma and cholangiocarcinoma were heterogeneous across countries, with interpretation limited by substantial variation in histologically unspecified cases. Rising liver cancer rates among older adults in historically low-incidence countries might suggest a shift from infectious to noncommunicable causes. In contrast, declines in younger adults in historically high-incidence countries may signal the positive impact of hepatitis and aflatoxin control. Strengthened, targeted prevention remains essential to prevent liver cancer globally.

items.title: Targeted liquid biopsy using CEUS to facilitate the release of ctDNA in colorectal liver metastasis.
items.abstract: Liquid biopsy as a non-invasive diagnosis tool for tumor genotyping, was limited by its low sensitivity. Ultrasound targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD) technique could temporarily alter tissue permeability, but its role in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) released remains poor understood. This study included mouse experiments and a prospective clinical study, aimed to investigate whether UTMD could increase the release of ctDNA and thus enhance the sensitivity of liquid biopsy. To establish the safety profile, H&E staining, PCR and Flow cytometric assays were conducted to evaluate liver injury and tumor dissemination after UTMD treatment. To evaluate UTMD-induced ctDNA release, droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to measure ctDNA copies at baseline and 5-30 min post-UTMD in BALB/c nude mice bearing liver metastases established with the human SW1463 colorectal cancer cell line (n = 28) and in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) (n = 10). In mouse models, UTMD under safety parameters (3∼3.3 MHz frequency, 2 cycles pulse length, 500 Hz PRF, 52.5%∼60% acoustic power and 0.5 MI) did not cause liver inflammation and tumor dissemination. UTMD treatment induced a transient, significant increase in human KRAS ctDNA copies (5-fold increase, P = 0.007), which returned to baseline within 30 min. In human participants with CRLM, sonication of the liver tumors resulted in a 2.2-fold increase (P = 0.045) in KRAS ctDNA mutant allele frequency measured 5 min after the procedure. These findings highlight the clinical utility of diagnostic ultrasound in liquid biopsy for detecting specific oncogene mutations in abdominal diseases, which are critical for personalized cancer therapy.

items.title: Robotic as routine approach for minimally invasive liver surgery: A single center experience with 277 robotic liver resections.
items.abstract: Robotic platforms aim to overcome laparoscopic limitations in hepatobiliary surgery. This study reports an initial experience with robotic liver resection (RLR), focusing on its application in a tertiary cancer center identifying predictors of conversion and postoperative complications. A retrospective analysis was performed on 277 RLRs (2017-2025). Analyzed data included Iwate difficulty scores, operative variables, and 90-days outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression analyzed factors associated with surgical outcomes. The cohort included 277 RLRs in 273 patients (93.9% malignant disease). Mean operative time was 207 min and blood loss 169.2 mL. Major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥3) occurred in 7.6%, with a 0.4% mortality and 95.3% R0 resection rate. Conversion rate was 10.1% (2.5% for technical reasons). Advanced Iwate scores significantly predicted higher conversion (p = 0.005) and longer operative times (p = 0.001). Regression identified tumor number (p = 0.036) and Iwate score (p = 0.003) as independent predictors for conversion, while CCI was linked to complications (p = 0.035). RLR is a safe and effective tool for complex oncological scenarios, including patients with prior surgeries or bilobar disease. While procedural complexity and tumor burden increase conversion risk, RLR maintains low morbidity and high radicality, supporting its routine adoption for both minor and major resections.
